narrative.text:
I’ll compare the fork with current upstream and the open PRs, then write the proposed split to the evidence report. I won’t change repository files or make a commit.Current upstream is still `ca8f6b1`. It already has general group-DM support, write allow-lists and DM-disable controls; the fork adds opt-in, exact-conversation authorization.

The main split constraint is avoiding a partially enforced policy. I’m planning inert preparatory PRs, with activation only after history, inbound events, writes and attachment fetches are covered. I also found two compatibility details to flag: explicit policy overrides the legacy DM switches, and the fork’s group-DM display changes also affect no-policy mode.The report is complete. It proposes four base-policy PRs, a separate named-group-DM PR, and an optional public-pin fallback PR, with size estimates and tests for each.

It also flags the compatibility decisions and known fetch-mock leak. The worktree remains clean; no code or commit was made. A report-writing quoting error was corrected and disclosed in the evidence.
